transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (as listed): Morgan Ellis, Priya Nair, Ethan Zhou (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Marcus Hale, Sofia Park, Jon Ruiz (MapleCore)

Summary:
Quick standup to align on runbook items, SSO/KMS questions, sample traffic for performance tuning, and plan bench tests for a private deployment. Agree on owners and dates; follow-up deliverables to enable week-of bench testing.

Topics covered:
- Integration runbook and required infra artifacts
- Auth (SSO/SAML) and identity mapping
- Networking (VPC peering / NAT / firewall rules)
- Data handling, KMS, audit logs
- Bench testing approach and SLOs (p99 latency, throughput)
- Next steps and owners

[00:00] Morgan (Redwood AE): All right folks, thanks for jumping on. I think we've got about 50 minutes, so we'll do a quick round for intros, then go through the integration playbook milestones. Priya and Ethan from our side, and from MapleCore — Lena, Marcus, Sofia, Jon — thanks for making time.

[00:28] Lena (MapleCore): Yep, hi all. We're excited to get the runbook nailed down. Our timeline is pretty tight; we want a pilot in staging before Thanksgiving, so about three weeks.

[00:45] Priya (CSM): Great, that's helpful. We'll align priorities to that timeline. Quick clarifying question — is staging on-prem or cloud?

[01:05] Marcus (DevOps): Staging is AWS, us-east-1, inside our default VPC but we use a transitive VPC design. We will need VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your recommendations.

[01:30] Ethan (SE): Cool. For private deployments we generally do VPC peering where possible, but PrivateLink can be used for stricter network boundaries. The runbook includes both patterns. We'll need your account IDs and a peering CIDR. Also, a heads-up — if you need egress through a proxy, that changes the bench test a bit.

[01:55] Sofia (PM): On features: our first use case is customer support agent augmentation — short prompts, high QPS, need p99 under 350ms for 256 token contexts. Cost also matters.

[02:15] Morgan: Understood. We'll map that to a model variant and batching profile in the runbook. Ethan, maybe speak to caching and batching?

[02:30] Ethan: Sure — for short prompts we recommend prefix caching and a small batch window to hit cost targets without blowing latency. The K-V cache — sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in notes — it's a small prefix cache for identical prompts. We'll share a config suggestion. Also note quantization recommendations if you're cost-sensitive.

[03:00] Jon (Security): Quick security note: we need SOC2 type II evidence, audit log export capability, and details on key management. We prefer our KMS; can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM?

[03:20] Priya: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS. We'll share the KMS integration doc. Also you'll get audit logs to your SIEM; we have parity with common formats but we'll confirm a sample export.

[03:45] Marcus: And SSO — we use Okta. Do you support SAML 2.0 metadata exchange? Any gotchas mapping teams/roles to RBAC?

[04:00] Ethan: We do SAML 2.0 and SSO. The runbook includes an attribute mapping example. FWIW sometimes attributes are named differently — e.g., group vs groups or role vs roles — so expect a little mapping. We'll provide a working example.

[04:25] Morgan: Great. Let's walk the runbook checklist, high level: infra prerequisites, network (VPC peering), identities, keys, sample prompts & traffic, bench test plan, then go/no-go gating.

[04:45] Ethan: I'll open the runbook link in the deck — (audio) — ok, slide 3 is infra requirements: minimum instance types, storage for model cache if private, and port rules. Note for model cache we recommend ephemeral NVMe for performance.

[05:12] Lena: For our staging fleet we can add NVMe to two instances. Cost is fine for the bench.

[05:30] Morgan: Perfect. Next the bench test — target metrics? Customer asked about p99 <350ms at X QPS. We should capture intended request distribution.

[05:45] Sofia: We'll compile a top-50 prompt list that reflects real usage. Mostly short context with some 512 token flows for escalation. Typical QPS estimate: 120 steady, peaks to 300 during high load.

[06:05] Ethan: OK, that'll inform batch sizes. For 120 QPS steady the runtime will favor continuous batching with small windows; at peaks we might need to scale to additional replicas. Bench test will simulate steady + ramp + spike. I'll draft the scenario.

[06:30] Marcus: For network, our firewall team requires exact CIDR ranges for allow-listing. Can you provide static egress IPs?

[06:45] Priya: For Dedicated/Private we support static egress via NAT gateways on the customer's side; we'll provide the expected endpoints. Note hosted mode has shared IPs and isn't suitable for your compliance ask.

[07:05] Jon: About data retention — do you keep logs or payloads? We need to ensure PII isn't retained unless allowed.

[07:18] Ethan: By default for Private, logs remain in your environment; for hosted we have controls to redact or not store payloads. We'll send the data retention policy excerpt. There's also an option for token-level redaction.

[07:40] Morgan: Quick pause for questions.

[07:50] Lena: On SLA — what are typical latency SLOs for private vs hosted? If something goes wrong during ramp we need escalation path.

[08:05] Morgan: For Private, we align to contract-level SLOs; generally we aim for <200ms p50 and configured p99 goals depending on model and hardware. We'll include an escalation contact list. Priya will own the runbook delivery.

[08:30] Priya: I'll push the runbook draft to the shared folder by EOD tomorrow and include the SSO/KMS checklist.

[08:43] Marcus: Perfect. Also, any prebuilt Terraform/ARM for infra?

[08:55] Ethan: We have Terraform modules for VPC peering, security groups, and a sample helm chart if you prefer k8s. We'll send a repo link. Sometimes the k8s manifests use slightly different labels (the transcriber sometimes turns helm into 'helm' or 'help' — disregard).

[09:20] Sofia: For observability, can we get per-route token cost breakdowns? Our finance partner wants a cost forecast.

[09:35] Morgan: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns. We'll include a sample CSV export so your finance team can run forecasts.

[09:50] Jon: On encryption in transit — do you support mTLS?

[09:58] Ethan: mTLS is supported for Private endpoints. For hosted we use TLS 1.3. We'll include cert rotation guidance.

[10:15] Morgan: All right, time to align owners and due dates. Action item recap — Priya will share runbook and SSO doc by Monday (that's 2027-10-24). Ethan will craft bench test plan and initial SLOs by 2027-10-27. Lena/Marcus will provide VPC peering info and sample traffic by 2027-10-28.

[10:45] Marcus: One more thing — on the bench test, can you run with both quantized and non-quantized model variants? We want to see cost vs quality tradeoffs.

[11:00] Ethan: Yep — we'll include a 4-way matrix: baseline full-precision, quantized, cached scenario, and scaled-out baseline. We'll produce a short report with latency ceilings and token cost per 1k requests.

[11:20] Sofia: Should we include evals for quality regression? We have a small labeled set.

[11:30] Priya: Yes please. Send the labeled eval set; we'll run regressions as part of the bench and flag any >2% drop in accuracy on key intents.

[11:45] Morgan: Excellent. Any blockers left?

[11:52] Lena: Only internal approvals for peering and the security review calendar. We'll try to get approvals this week.

[12:05] Jon: We'll paste SOC2 docs to the shared folder and ping your security contact for anything missing.

[12:18] Morgan: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate the runbook and action-item list after the call. Next sync — propose a 30-minute bench planning session on 2027-10-27, anyone object?

[12:35] Marcus: Works for me.

[12:40] Lena: Works.

[12:45] Morgan: Great. Closing notes: Redwood to add a short checklist for 'go/no-go' criteria for staging -> pilot. Priya will track.

[12:55] (crosstalk, wrap up)

End transcript.
